summary.text: 24-year-old man with severe atopic dermatitis since infancy and moderate bronchial asthma since adolescence, with T2-high inflammation and sensitization to house dust mite and Alternaria. His mother had asthma. Prior glucocorticosteroids, topical therapy and cyclosporine (ineffective, poorly tolerated, stopped) and budesonide/formoterol plus montelukast had not controlled disease.

At presentation he had generalized eruptions, intense pruritus, irritability, sleep disturbance and periodic dyspnea, cough and wheezing, with erythema, lichenification, excoriations, occasional wheezes, SCORAD 103, DLQI 30, ACQ-5 2.8, AEC 1,000 cells/µl, total IgE 8,400 IU/ml, high mite and Alternaria sIgE and mild obstruction with positive bronchodilator response on spirometry.

Dupilumab 600 mg subcutaneously then 300 mg every 2 weeks was started, and subcutaneous AIT with house dust mite and Alternaria extracts began 8 weeks after the first injection while inhaled budesonide/formoterol was stepped down from 640/18 to 160/4.5 mcg/day.

Scores and IgE fell and allergen-specific IgG4 rose through 48 weeks, when he had sustained clinical remission (SCORAD 1, DLQI 0, ACQ-5 0), AEC 100 cells/µl, total IgE 450 IU/ml, and no treatment-related adverse effects were reported.
